dataset_metadata.title: United States Childhood and Adolescent Immunization Master Data
dataset_metadata.schedule_version: CDC child and adolescent schedule by age, July 2 2025 (compliant version)
dataset_metadata.schedule_version_note: CDC currently identifies the July 2, 2025 schedule as the current posted CDC schedule pursuant to the March 16, 2026 preliminary court order. AAP publishes a separate 2026 schedule. Keep authority/version configurable and verify current official guidance before production use.
dataset_metadata.age_calculation: Calculate age from date_of_birth using calendar months/years, not fixed 30-day months. Store recommended age windows separately from minimum age and minimum interval rules.
dataset_metadata.important_safety_note: This is an app-development reference dataset, not medical advice or an individualized vaccination order. A licensed clinician must determine eligibility, product, dose validity, catch-up timing, contraindications and precautions.

sources.title: Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule by Age (Compliant)
Vaccines and Other Immunizing Agents in the Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule
Recommended Childhood and Adolescent Immunization Schedule: United States, 2026

vaccines.name: Hepatitis B

conditional_rules.description: Infant born to HBsAg-positive or unknown-status mother requires time-critical birth prophylaxis and possible HBIG; follow perinatal protocol and clinician instructions.

vaccines.notes: Dose timing and birth weight/maternal HBsAg status affect the regimen. Do not use this simplified routine series to calculate perinatal prophylaxis.

vaccines.name: Rotavirus
vaccines.notes: First dose must be started by 14 weeks 6 days; no dose after 8 months 0 days. Product and prior doses determine series.

vaccines.name: Diphtheria, tetanus, and acellular pertussis
vaccines.notes: DTaP is for children younger than 7 years. Dose 4 may be given from 12 months if at least 6 months after dose 3; clinician/catch-up rules determine validity.

vaccines.name: Haemophilus influenzae type b
protects_against: invasive Haemophilus influenzae type b disease
vaccines.notes: Primary-series dose count depends on product. Mixed/unknown product histories need official catch-up rules.

vaccines.name: Pneumococcal conjugate

conditional_rules.description: Additional pneumococcal vaccination may be indicated for certain medical conditions, immunocompromising conditions, cochlear implant or cerebrospinal fluid leak; product and prior PCV/PPSV23 history determine plan.

vaccines.notes: Routine infant series and risk-based recommendations are distinct. Do not automatically add PPSV23 or extra PCV doses.

vaccines.name: Inactivated poliovirus
vaccines.notes: A fourth dose is not needed if the third dose was given at age 4 years or older and at least 6 months after the previous dose, subject to official rules.

vaccines.name: Influenza

routine_series.doses_per_season: 1 or 2 depending on age and prior influenza vaccination history

rules.if: age 6 months through 8 years and has not previously received at least 2 total influenza vaccine doses before July 1 of the current season
age 6 months through 8 years and previously received at least 2 qualifying doses

products: Live attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV; age/health restrictions apply)
vaccines.notes: Record influenza season/year and formulation. Annual product guidance changes; verify age indication and contraindications each season.

vaccines.name: COVID-19

routine_series.doses: Product-, age-, vaccination-history- and season-dependent; retrieve current-season schedule at administration time.

vaccines.notes: Do not hardcode a permanent dose count. Keep season, product, age eligibility, prior doses and current official guidance in a versioned rule set.

vaccines.name: Measles, mumps, and rubella

conditional_rules.description: An early dose may be recommended for infants 6–11 months for international travel or outbreak circumstances; it does not replace the routine 2-dose series.

vaccines.notes: Live vaccine; screen for contraindications and special circumstances.

vaccines.name: Varicella
vaccines.notes: For children younger than 13 years, routine interval is 3 months; a dose given at least 4 weeks after dose 1 may be accepted as valid under applicable guidance.

conditional_rules.description: Additional age-appropriate vaccination may be recommended for travel or specific risk groups; clinician review required.

vaccines.name: Tetanus, diphtheria, and acellular pertussis

conditional_rules.description: Children age 7 years or older who are not fully vaccinated with DTaP need an age-appropriate catch-up series; wound management may require additional doses.

vaccines.notes: Tdap is also used during each pregnancy, but maternal vaccination is outside this child record schedule.

vaccines.name: Human papillomavirus

dose_rules.if: series started before 15th birthday and not immunocompromised
series started at age 15 years or older OR immunocompromised
dose_rules.intervals: 0, 1–2, and 6 months; apply official minimum intervals

vaccines.notes: May begin at age 9. Use age at first dose and immunocompromised status to select 2- versus 3-dose series.

conditional_rules.description: Certain high-risk children may need MenACWY beginning at 2 months, with product-specific multi-dose schedules and boosters.

vaccines.name: Meningococcal B

routine_series.dose_count: Product- and indication-dependent; commonly 2-dose series for healthy adolescents under shared clinical decision-making; high-risk schedules may differ.

conditional_rules.description: Certain medical conditions, complement inhibitor use, asplenia, outbreak or exposure may warrant MenB at younger ages or a different series.

vaccines.notes: Do not interchange products within a series unless current official guidance explicitly permits.

vaccines.name: RSV monoclonal antibody protection
protects_against: respiratory syncytial virus lower respiratory tract disease

routine_series.first_rsv_season: One dose for eligible infants, depending on maternal RSV vaccination status and timing; generally given shortly before or during first RSV season.
routine_series.second_rsv_season: One dose for certain high-risk children 8 through 19 months entering their second RSV season.

conditional_rules.description: Most infants do not need infant RSV antibody if maternal RSV vaccine was given at least 14 days before delivery; exceptions and clinical factors apply.
Second-season protection is limited to defined high-risk groups.

vaccines.notes: Store separately from vaccines because this is a monoclonal antibody. Seasonal eligibility and product guidance must be refreshed.

vaccines.name: Dengue

conditional_rules.description: Only for children living in dengue-endemic areas with laboratory-confirmed previous dengue infection, per applicable authorization and guidance.

vaccines.notes: Not a routine vaccine for all US children; geographic eligibility and documented prior infection are essential.

vaccines.name: Mpox

routine_series.age: Use only when currently authorized/recommended for the child's age and circumstance; routine CDC child schedule lists risk-based guidance.

conditional_rules.description: Consider only for eligible exposure/risk circumstances under current public-health guidance; pediatric use may require specific authorization or specialist/public-health direction.

vaccines.notes: Do not assign universally to all 18-year-olds; verify current age authorization and public-health guidance.

vaccines.name: Pneumococcal polysaccharide

conditional_rules.description: May be indicated for certain children with qualifying medical conditions or risk factors; sequence depends on prior PCV products and current recommendations.

vaccines.notes: Not part of the routine healthy-infant series.

combination_vaccines.typical_use: Primary infant doses; product-specific age and series rules apply.
combination_vaccines.notes: Do not create three separate injection records. Create one administration event linked to three component dose credits.

combination_vaccines.typical_use: Infant primary series; product-specific age and series rules apply.
combination_vaccines.notes: One administration event can satisfy component doses when each component dose is valid.

combination_vaccines.typical_use: Booster dose in the 4–6-year age range when indicated.
combination_vaccines.notes: Check age, prior doses and product-specific licensing.

combination_vaccines.typical_use: Booster dose in the 4–6-year age range when indicated.
combination_vaccines.notes: Check age, prior doses and product-specific licensing.

combination_vaccines.typical_use: Infant primary series; not used for every booster dose.
combination_vaccines.notes: Product-specific rules apply, including Hib/HepB dose credit.

combination_vaccines.typical_use: May be used for eligible second-year or preschool doses.
combination_vaccines.notes: Discuss febrile seizure considerations for first dose in young children; clinician selects product.

combination_vaccines.typical_use: Certain adolescents/young adults when both components are indicated.
combination_vaccines.notes: Use only according to current age indication and product-specific guidance; component series remain separately tracked.

schedule_rules.routine_due_date_calculation: Add calendar months/years to date_of_birth for age-based recommendations. A due window is a range, not a single exact date. Store earliest_valid_date, recommended_start_date, recommended_end_date and latest_routine_date separately.
schedule_rules.dose_validity: A dose administered too early may not count. Validate minimum age and minimum interval using the current official schedule and applicable grace-period rules before marking a series complete.
schedule_rules.catch_up: Do not restart a vaccine series because of an extended interval. Use the current CDC catch-up table and product-specific notes. This dataset intentionally does not encode every catch-up branch.
schedule_rules.unknown_history: Mark history as unknown/unverified and route to clinician review; do not assume zero doses or mark a series complete.
schedule_rules.prematurity: Most vaccines are scheduled by chronological age; HepB birth-dose rules and selected clinical circumstances require special handling.
schedule_rules.combination_products: Record one physical administration event with multiple vaccine_component_credits. Validate each credited component independently.
schedule_rules.annual_vaccines: Generate a new influenza season record each year; do not model annual influenza as one lifelong dose series.
schedule_rules.conditional_rules: Do not automatically schedule risk-based, travel-related, outbreak-related, shared-decision or maternal-status-dependent immunizations without the required eligibility data and clinician approval.

status_definitions.upcoming: Outside the due window and not yet administered.
status_definitions.due: Within the recommended due window and not yet administered.
status_definitions.overdue: Past the recommended window and not yet administered; this is a reminder state, not a clinical validity decision.
status_definitions.completed: Administration recorded and dose validity confirmed.
status_definitions.deferred: Temporarily postponed; store reason and clinician follow-up.
status_definitions.not_indicated: Clinician determined this dose is not indicated for this child.
status_definitions.unknown_history: Prior vaccination status cannot be confirmed.
